clues: This city sits in the south of a Mexican state. It lies a long way from the state capital, Xalapa.
The weather here stays warm all year. Its rains come in summer and in autumn.
In nineteen sixty, it got its own local government. Its land had once been part of a nearby town.
Its present name honors a local martyr for land rights. The town took that name in nineteen twenty-five.
Each December, this town celebrates the Virgin of Guadalupe. She is the patron saint of this town.
